Drop levels that are empty at every site, for models

Source: R/model_levels.R
ds.omop.drop_empty_levels.Rd

Published factor columns share one level set across sites, including levels that no site uses (declared vocabulary lists, calendars, level ranges). A level empty at every site gives an all-zero design column, so a pooled ds.glm() fails as singular. This makes a copy for models whose factor columns keep only the levels that hold a value at some site, identical at every site and in the same order; each copy keeps its own rows and values.

Usage

ds.omop.drop_empty_levels(
  x,
  columns = NULL,
  newobj = paste0(x, "_model"),
  symbol = "omop",
  conns = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Character; a published in-memory table on every site (a recipe_execute() output, for example).

columns

Optional character vector of factor columns; by default every published concept, category or calendar column (the columns the servers reconciled; other factors, such as legacy age bands, are left as they are).

newobj

Character; the server-side name of the copy.

symbol

Character; the OMOP session symbol.

conns

DSI connections; defaults to the session's connections.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with one row per column: levels before, kept and status.

Details

Which levels hold a value at a site is an observed-level release: each site reports it under DataSHIELD's factor-level rule (nfilter.levels.max and nfilter.levels.density, as ds.asFactor does), without counts. A column whose levels in use fail that rule at some site keeps all its levels; group it first (omop_category_recode(), omop_category_rollup()), which also suits models better.

The copy is for analysis. Its dropped columns no longer carry the dsOMOP presentation contract, so publish again from the recipe for anything else.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
recipe_execute(recipe, out = c(study = "D"))
ds.omop.drop_empty_levels("D", newobj = "D_model")
dsBaseClient::ds.glm(died ~ cause_of_death, data = "D_model", family = "binomial")
} # }
